title: Author + implement PROP-NNN: meta-audit of all scheduled agents for required-output-artifact LLM-skip vulnerability; ship structural enforcement (pre-push hooks) where applicable
background:
We now have evidence the 'LLM agent narrates success on a step it didn't actually complete' pattern is NOT limited to one agent. Two confirmed instances in the past 4 days:

  - **PROP-076 lint gate bypass (decider)**: shipped 2026-06-03; agent skipped the gate invocation on 3 decider pushes (38deae25 / f52d3ae0 / 196dde8d). Discovered by tinker forensics on 2026-06-06T05:04Z. Fixed structurally via PROP-080's pre-push hook (shipped 2026-06-06T05:43Z).

  - **prune-integrity report-write skip (today)**: 2026-06-06T08:06Z agent ran the prune script (load-bearing data work landed in commit `b8e3c000`), narrated 'Run report: monitor/integrity/prune-integrity-runs/run-2026-06-06T08-06-36Z.json' in its log, but the report file is HTTP 404 on origin/main — never committed. The agent's clone got `rm -rf`'d after the data commit, taking the unstaged report file with it. Permanently lost for today.

The pattern: agent's prompt has multiple sequential bash actions; the LLM completes the load-bearing one(s) and reports success, but skips a non-load-bearing 'audit trail' or 'verification' step. The skip is invisible at agent runtime; only later forensics (tinker replay, or integrity catch-up) reveals it. Same shape as the PROP-074 dome-mirror Step 4c saga (six prompt iterations failed; architectural separation finally fixed it).

Operator hypothesis: there are likely MORE instances of this bug class across the 12 enabled scheduled agents. Each agent has at least one 'required output artifact' (run report, sentinel, summary file, lint annotation, etc.) that the prompt documents as expected. If the LLM is skipping ANY of them silently, we have an undocumented blind spot.

Goal: tinker enumerates all scheduled agents, identifies their required output artifacts per their prompt, replays recent runs to detect silent skips, and ships structural enforcement (pre-push hook pattern from PROP-080) for the vulnerable subset.

operator_decision.rationale: Two confirmed cases in 4 days suggests this is a class of bug, not a one-off. PROP-080 proved the structural-enforcement pattern works; applying it preemptively where applicable is cheaper than waiting for each agent's silent-skip to be discovered (one at a time) by integrity. Cost is bounded because there are 12 agents and most produce 1-2 required artifacts each; per-agent audit + hook is ~20 min of forensic work.

requested_work: Step 1 — Enumerate the 12 enabled scheduled agents from CLAUDE.md's Monitoring Pipeline table or `list_scheduled_tasks` output. For each, read its prompt file (`monitor/prompts/<agent>.md`) and identify every 'required output artifact' the prompt documents — i.e., any file/path the prompt says the agent MUST produce per run. Common shapes: run reports (e.g., `monitor/integrity/*-runs/run-*.json`), sentinels (e.g., `monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-*.json`), summaries (e.g., `monitor/decisions/latest-decider-summary.txt`), audit-trail JSONLs (e.g., `monitor/tinker/queue-history.jsonl`), per-cycle artifacts.

Step 2 — For each (agent, required_artifact) pair, classify the protection category:
  (A) ALREADY STRUCTURAL — protected by a pre-push hook or equivalent enforcement (e.g., PROP-080 for decider close-records).
  (B) WORKSPACE-RESCUE — workspace-owned file rescued by workspace-sync's universal-pusher if missed (e.g., `latest-decider-summary.txt`, `latest-baby-summary.txt`).
  (C) VULNERABLE-CLONE-PUSH — agent pushes from its own clone; if the LLM skips the artifact-write or git-add step, the artifact is lost when the clone is rm'd. THIS IS THE BUG CLASS.
  (D) BENIGN — artifact is optional / regenerable / not required.
  Per-agent classification table goes in PROP-NNN's evidence section.

Step 3 — For each (C)-classified pair, replay recent runs (last 7-14 days of commits from that agent) to check: did the expected artifact actually land in git? Forensic technique parallel to tinker's 2026-06-06T05:04Z discovery — fetch the agent's commits, parse for the artifact path, verify each is present (or correctly-missing per the artifact's semantics). Cite the recurrence rate per agent in the evidence section.

Step 4 — Author monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-required-artifacts-structural-enforcement.json. Required sections: title, problem statement (cite this directive + the 2 known cases + the per-agent classification table from Step 2), recurrence findings from Step 3, proposed fix per vulnerable agent (the hook design or alternative), Q-OPs if any, verification_pattern, files_touched list, estimated_loc.

Step 5 — Operator pre-approves the following design directions; tinker should pick per agent:
  (a) PREFERRED for vulnerable agents pushing from clone: PROP-080-style pre-push hook that verifies expected artifact(s) are staged before allowing the push. Hook would refuse push if a required artifact path is in the agent's prompt's 'expected output' list but NOT in `git diff --cached --name-only` output. Simplest, mirrors PROP-080's proven structural pattern.
  (b) Alternative for low-vulnerability agents: keep prompt-level only + add a post-push integrity check (next-day forensics that fires an ISS if the artifact is missing). Detective rather than preventive.
  (c) Shared script: ship `monitor/scripts/lint-required-artifacts.js` that takes the expected-artifact list as a flag (e.g. `--required path1,path2`) and exits 1 if any are missing from staged. Wire it as the hook contents for each vulnerable agent. Reduces per-agent code; one canonical lint script for all.
  Operator preference: (c) for code reuse — one script, multiple hooks. Hook in each vulnerable agent's clone-setup invokes it with the right --required list.

Step 6 — Tinker self-applies per the PROP-076/077/078/079/080 pattern: write proposal, implement same run if total LOC across all per-agent prompt edits + the shared script + (any) install logic is <150, verification pattern passes for each vulnerable agent. Hold for operator review if scope balloons past 150 LOC or if a Q-OP surfaces (likely: 'which agents found vulnerable, and what's their required-artifact list?').

Step 7 — Validation per agent: for each agent that gets a hook installed, simulate a 'missed artifact' scenario (stage data commit without the artifact, attempt push, verify hook refuses with clear error). Document each simulation in PROP-NNN's verification section.

Step 8 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-NNN.json status='implemented' with implementation_commit/at/run + per-agent rollout list. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. Update PROP-080's status note to reference PROP-NNN as the generalization (do NOT supersede — PROP-080 remains the canonical decider-specific implementation).

Step 9 — Manually copy edited prompts + lint script to FUSE so the next session-bootstrap for each vulnerable agent picks up the new hook. dome-mirror will propagate within ~30 min on its :30 cron, but manual sync is the safe bootstrap path.

Step 10 — Operator follow-up reminder in PROP-NNN's post-deployment plan: monitor the next 3-7 days of each newly-hooked agent for either (a) zero new same-class artifact-missing findings (success) or (b) the hook firing legitimately (still success — caught a skip before push). If the hook starts blocking too aggressively or false-positives appear, that's a Q-OP for next round.
non_goals: Do NOT touch PROP-080's decider hook unless Step 3 forensics surface a regression. PROP-080 is the working precedent.
Do NOT proliferate new 'required artifacts' that weren't already documented in agent prompts. Stay scoped to artifacts the prompt ALREADY says are expected output.
Do NOT extend to workspace-sync's universal-pusher logic. That's a separate surface (it's the rescue mechanism for category (B)) and was hardened by PROP-077 + PROP-078 last week.
Do NOT add hooks for one-off scripts (build.js, push-via-api.js outside of the lint-gate context PROP-080 already added). Stay scoped to scheduled-agent SKILL.md / prompt files.

Do NOT block on retroactive recovery of today's missing prune-integrity report (run-2026-06-06T08-06-36Z.json). It's permanently lost (clone rm'd). The next prune run tomorrow will produce a fresh report; one-day gap in audit history is acceptable.
Do NOT scope to agents currently disabled (sloppytoppy-score, sloppytoppy-rewrite, etc.). Stay focused on the 12 enabled ones plus dome-mirror (since we know it's reliable post-PROP-074).

expected_output: (1) monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-required-artifacts-structural-enforcement.json with status='implemented'. (2) Either monitor/scripts/lint-required-artifacts.js (if design (c) is picked) OR per-agent hook scripts (if (a) per-agent). (3) Edits to each vulnerable agent's prompt installing the pre-push hook at clone-setup time. (4) Per-agent simulation evidence in PROP-NNN's verification section. (5) This directive at status='completed'. (6) FUSE-synced files.
estimated_effort: ~90-120 min Opus. Step 1-2 enumeration + classification (~25 min). Step 3 per-agent forensic replay is the longest piece (~40 min, depending on how many vulnerable agents found). Step 4-5 proposal + implementation (~30 min). Step 7-9 validation + lifecycle (~15 min).
priority_note: HIGH — meta-pattern generalization. Each day we don't catch the broader class, we risk more silent skips landing in production state. PROP-080 was the proof-of-concept; this PROP is the scale-up. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs.
